claims.text: A market economic system is an economic system in which resources are allocated through the price mechanism: private ownership, the decisions of households and firms, and prices formed by demand and supply determine what is produced, how it is produced and for whom.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: The features of a market economic system are private ownership of most resources, production decisions taken by households and firms rather than by government, the profit motive as the driving incentive, and prices that move freely to allocate resources.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: In a market economic system the three questions - what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce - are answered by consumer spending and producer choices, with no central authority directing resources.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Prices in a market system act as signals and incentives: a rising price signals scarcity and the chance of profit, which tends to draw firms and resources into an industry, while a falling price tends to push resources out.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: An advantage of the market system is consumer sovereignty: consumers direct resources by choosing what to buy, so firms tend to produce what consumers want, because that is where sales and profit are found.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: An advantage of the market system is that competition among firms tends to keep prices and costs down and widens choice, because a firm that charges more than its rivals for a similar product tends to lose customers.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: An advantage of the market system is that the profit motive and the price mechanism tend to move resources toward their most valued uses without a central plan, because resources flow to the uses where prices and profits are highest.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A disadvantage of the market system is an unequal distribution of income: rewards follow scarce skills and ownership of resources, so incomes tend to differ widely between households.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A disadvantage of the market system is that goods that cannot easily be priced and sold to individual buyers, such as street lighting, tend to be under-provided, because a firm cannot charge the people who benefit without paying.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A disadvantage of the market system is that goods which impose costs on others may still be produced where they are profitable, because a firm chasing profit may ignore the harm its production causes to third parties.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A disadvantage of the market system is that it may fail to provide work for everyone who wants it, because production depends on expected profit rather than on the need for jobs.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: An advantage of the market system is that the profit motive gives firms an incentive to use resources efficiently and to innovate, because cutting costs and offering new or better products tends to raise profit, while firms that waste resources tend to lose customers to rivals.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A disadvantage of the market system is that where one firm or a few firms dominate a market, they may abuse that power by charging higher prices, restricting output, or offering poorer quality and less choice, because consumers have few alternatives to turn to.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A disadvantage of the market system is that when demand moves away from an industry, its workers and other resources may stay unemployed for a long time, because factors of production often cannot move easily between occupations and places.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Countries rely on the market system to different degrees: the United States relies heavily on private firms and prices, Germany combines markets with extensive social protection, and Vietnam moved from central planning towards markets from the late 1980s, after which farm output rose as farmers responded to prices.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
